Simple Problems
T–S · Question 1 — M1 Recall
You arrive at Solaris Manufacturing for a client visit. The receptionist says: "Good morning! Who are you here to see?" — What do you say? Use: My name is… / I'm a [job] / I have a meeting with…
S–S · Question 2 — M4 Recall
You don't know where the meeting room is. Ask your partner using there is/are and a preposition: "Excuse me — is there a meeting room on this floor? Where is it?"
Class · Question 3 — M5 Recall
You're in the elevator with a colleague you don't know well. Break the ice: one thing you can do, one thing you like about the company, one thing you need this week. 3 sentences.
Teacher Note — Error Harvest
Collect 3–5 student sentences on the board. Don't correct — circle structures you'll revisit in §5. This is warm activation, not testing.
⚡ Quick Win — 20 seconds
Say this out loud: "My name is [your name]. I'm a [your job] at [your company]. There is a meeting room on the third floor. I can speak English." — Four modules. One breath.
5 min · 3 recall questions · Badge 🏢 when done
§2
Speaking · Arriving at Solaris Manufacturing
3 rounds · Reception → Elevator → Problem · Full integration context
8–10 min
T–S
Scene: Reception desk, Solaris Manufacturing, Celaya.
Receptionist (teacher): "Good morning! Do you have an appointment?"
Student: introduce yourself, state your company, say who you're meeting. Use to be + possessives + Simple Present.

"Good morning! My name is Ana García. I'm a coordinator at Lumina Finance. I have a meeting with Mr. Torres at 10 AM. Here's my ID."

to be + job · possessive · Simple Present "have" · ID culture in Mexican companies

S–S
Scene: Elevator. You're going to the 4th floor.
A colleague you don't know steps in. Make small talk for 30 seconds — ONE thing you like about the company, ONE thing you need today, and ask them one Wh-question.

"Hey! I like the new cafeteria. I need a visitor badge — mine is at reception. What floor are you going to?"

like + noun · need + noun · Wh-question · all natural in 3 sentences

Class
Scene: You have a problem. Choose ONE: (a) The printer is broken. (b) The meeting room is full. (c) Your badge doesn't work. Report the problem using there is/are + can't + need. Go around the class — each student a different problem.

"Excuse me — there's a problem with the printer. It's on the second floor, next to the meeting room. I can't print my documents. I need help, please."

there is + preposition + can't + need — all five modules in one problem sentence

Teacher Note — Integration Check
After Round 3, ask: "Which module did each sentence come from?" Students identify to be (M1), Simple Present (M2), adjectives (M3), there is/prepositions (M4), can/need (M5). Visual reminder that M6 is not new — it's everything assembled.

Teacher Note — GT Original: "floor" Pronunciation Trap
"floor" /flɔːr/ — NOT "flo-or" with two syllables. One syllable, rhymes with "more". Drill: "first floor / second floor / third floor / fourth floor" — faster each round. This word appears in EVERY office interaction.

Model: "The reception is on the first floor. You need a badge to enter. The elevator is next to the stairs."

§4
Colloquial · 4 Real Phrases for the Office
Reception · elevator · problems · professional small talk in English
5 min
"I'm here to see [name]."
The standard phrase at any corporate reception in English. Replaces everything else.
"Good morning — I'm here to see Mr. Torres."
"It doesn't work." / "It's not working."
The most useful problem phrase. Works for any broken equipment — printer, badge, screen, elevator.
"The badge reader isn't working — can you help me?"
"After you." / "Go ahead."
Elevator and door etiquette in English-speaking corporate culture. Simple, memorable, professional.
[Elevator door opens] "After you!" — [Colleague] "Thank you!"
"Bear with me." / "One moment, please."
When you need a few seconds to think, find something, or process in English. Buys you time gracefully.
"Bear with me — I need to find my badge." (GT Original!)
Teacher Note — Drill Sequence (2 min)
Teacher plays receptionist. Student arrives: "Good morning — I'm here to see [name]." Teacher: "One moment please." Student: "Of course — after you." Quick 3-person chain. The four phrases in one natural exchange.

Grammar · Integration Review — All 5 Modules
Problem → Tool format · Reception context · Activities + Quick Poll · Badge 🏢
10–12 min
🚨 Real Situation — First Day at a New Company
It's your first day at Vertex Logistics as a new engineer. In 60 seconds you need to: tell the receptionist who you are → ask where your desk is → say what you can do → say what you need.
"Soy ingeniero / No sé dónde está mi escritorio / Puedo usar SAP / Necesito mi gafete"
❓ How do you say all four — in English?
✅ Four Tools — One Per Module
M1 → "I'm an engineer at Vertex." — to be + a/an + job
M4 → "Where is my desk? / Is there a desk for me?" — there is/are + Wh-question
M5 → "I can use SAP." — can + base verb
M5 → "I need my badge." — need + noun
ModuleStructureReception exampleCommon error
M1 — to be I am / She is / They are "I'm Ana García. I'm a coordinator." "I am coordinator" ✗→ need a/an before job
M2 — Simple Present I work / She works / Do you…? "I work in the operations department." "She work here" ✗→ 3rd person -s always
M4 — there is/are There is a… / There are… "Is there a meeting room on this floor?" "Is there meeting room?" ✗→ need article a/an
M5 — can/need I can use… / I need a… "I can't print — I need paper." "I can to print" ✗→ can + BASE verb, no "to"
⚠️ The 4 errors that kill professional English — correct every time:
✘ "I am coordinator" → ✅ I am a coordinator — always a/an before singular jobs
✘ "She work here" → ✅ She works here — 3rd person S, no exceptions
✘ "Is there meeting room?" → ✅ Is there a meeting room? — article in questions too
✘ "I can to use SAP" → ✅ I can use SAP — base verb after can, never "to"

🗣️ Micro-Speaking — 60 seconds
You're the new employee. Tell your partner: who you are (M1) + what you do (M2) + where your desk is NOT (M4) + what you can/can't do (M5). 4 sentences, 4 modules.
✏️ Activity B — True or False? Reception Rules
"Is there a cafeteria?" — correct way to ask about facilities.
"She don't work here" — correct negative in Simple Present for 3rd person.
"I'm an engineer" uses the article AN correctly before a vowel sound.
"The elevator is between the stairs and the reception" uses a preposition correctly.
§6
Listening · First Day at Vertex Logistics
Ana García arrives · Integration of all 5 modules · 4 questions · Badge 🎧
8–10 min
Ana's First Day — Vertex Logistics, Celaya
A1.1 · M6 · S1A · Voice: Juliet (ElevenLabs) · 128 kbps
0:00 0:00

Good morning! My name is Ana García, and today is my first day at Vertex Logistics here in Celaya. I'm a new project coordinator. I'm very happy to be here!

I arrive at 8:45 AM. The reception is on the ground floor — it's next to the main entrance. There is a security guard in front of the door, and there are two receptionists at the desk. I sign in and show my ID. The receptionist gives me a visitor badge.

My new office is on the fourth floor. I take the elevator — it's between the stairs and the cafeteria. In the elevator, I meet my new colleague, David. He's tall and friendly. He's an operations manager. "Good morning! I'm David. After you!" he says. "Thank you!" I say. "I'm Ana — it's nice to meet you!"

There's a small problem: my badge doesn't work on the fourth floor. The door is closed and I can't open it. "Bear with me," says David. He calls reception on his phone. "Hi — there's a problem with Ana's badge. It doesn't work on the fourth floor. Can you fix it, please?" The receptionist says: "Of course! One moment."

My desk is in a big open office. There are twelve desks in total. The printer is next to my desk, and there's a window behind me — the view is great! I like the office. I need a computer password and a company email, but I don't have them yet. My manager says: "Don't worry — everything is available this afternoon."

It's a good first day. I can speak English — a little. I can use Excel. I can't use the new system yet, but I can learn. I'm ready!

📎 ElevenLabs: Voice — Ana (American English) · Speed 0.78 · Pitch 1.0 · A1.1 M6 S1A · ~185 words · All 5 module structures integrated

Teacher Note — Pre-listening Integration Task
Before playing: write on board — M1 / M2 / M3 / M4 / M5. Students listen once and mark which modules they hear. After: "Where did you hear to be? Simple Present? there is/are? adjectives? can?" This turns a comprehension exercise into a module map exercise.
1. Where is the reception at Vertex Logistics?
2. What is the problem with Ana's badge?
3. True or False: Ana can use the new company system on her first day.
4. True or False: David is friendly and works in operations.

Speaking Cards — Real Interaction Scenarios
6 office situations · 30 seconds · speak first, think second
Card 1 / 6
CARD 1 OF 6
You arrive at a new client's office. Introduce yourself at reception — name, company, who you're meeting.
M1: "My name is… / I'm a… / I'm here to see…"
CARD 2 OF 6
The elevator is full. Describe the scene: how many people are there, where are they going, what do you do?
M4: "There are… people. / The elevator is… / I can…"
CARD 3 OF 6
A visitor asks where the cafeteria is. Give clear directions using prepositions from M4.
M4: "It's on the… floor / next to… / in front of… / turn left"
CARD 4 OF 6
It's Monday morning. Tell a colleague 3 things about your work week — what you usually do, when, and how often.
M2: "I usually… / I always… on Mondays / I never…"
CARD 5 OF 6
Report a problem: the meeting room is full AND the printer is broken. What do you need? What can you do?
M4+M5: "There isn't… / The … is broken / I need… / I can…"
CARD 6 OF 6 ⭐
You are Ana on her first day. Introduce yourself to a new colleague in the elevator — everything about you in 5 sentences.
All modules: name + job + routine + skills + what you need today
